lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Supervised application: emergency and urgent-help procedures

objective: Learners rehearse stating a problem clearly, with context and what's needed, in an urgent-help communication drill with a trusted adult, so clear communication under pressure is practiced ahead of time rather than attempted for the first time during an actual emergency.
scenario: Using a provided fictional urgent scenario, the learner rehearses out loud with a trusted adult what they would say to get help — stating the problem, the location or context, and what's needed — explicitly framed as a communication-clarity drill, never as a substitute for actually contacting real emergency services in a real emergency.
safetyNotes: This is a communication-clarity drill using a fictional scenario; it is never a real emergency contact and must never involve actually contacting emergency services as practice.
No audio or video recording is made; the adult gives live feedback and the learner writes notes afterward.
If a learner has an actual urgent concern, this lesson is not the pathway for it — they should tell a trusted adult immediately and separately from this exercise.

simulationAlternative.description: If no adult is available to role-play, the learner writes both sides of the conversation as a script, then reads only their own side aloud once and self-checks it against the same look-fors.

tasks.directions: Before practicing, write down why clear, short sentences matter more than usual in an urgent moment.

prompts.text: Why might short, clear sentences matter even more than usual when someone needs to explain an urgent problem quickly?

tasks.directions: With your adult, rehearse stating the fictional problem, context, and need clearly.

prompts.text: I clearly stated what the problem was.
I clearly stated the location or context.
I clearly stated what was needed.

tasks.directions: Revise your script based on feedback and write the improved version.

prompts.text: Write your revised version of the urgent-help script, and explain what you changed to make it clearer or faster to say.
What's one thing that would help you stay clear and calm enough to actually say this if the moment were real?

remediation: If the script is too vague to actually act on (missing the problem, the context, or the specific need), reteach the three-part structure explicitly with one modeled example, then have the learner rebuild their own script to include all three parts.
extension: Have the learner adapt the same three-part structure for a version where they are speaking on behalf of someone else who cannot speak for themselves in the fictional scenario, and explain what changes.
